 Order
Raja Vijayaraghavan V, J.
The instant report of the Sabarimala Special Commissioner pertains to the delay in obtaining laboratory test results of honey samples collected from the Sannidhanam.

The Commissioner has reported that, in order to obtain clarity at the earliest regarding the quality, safety, and usability of the honey that has been kept apart, it is imperative to receive the laboratory analysis of the samples collected on 26.11.2025 without further delay.
A further query has also been raised as to whether the quantity of 1,260 litres of honey presently kept segregated in the main store is fit for use.

sentences.text:
By order dated 09.01.2026, this Court had suo motu impleaded the Chief Government Analyst,
Government Analyst Laboratory, Vanchiyoor, and issued directions to furnish the report with respect to the samples in question.
3. In compliance with the aforesaid directions, the report of the Food Analyst has been placed before this Court.

It is evident from the report that, except for a marginal increase in moisture content--measured at 21.20% by mass as against the prescribed standard of 20.0% by mass--all other parameters conform to the standards prescribed.

The Food Analyst has opined that since the moisture content marginally exceeds the permissible limit, the honey does not strictly conform to the standards stipulated under Regulation SSCR NO. 2 OF 2026     :4:   2026:KER:2813 2.8.3(1) of the Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives)
Regulations, 2011.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: However, it is specifically noted that the deviation is limited solely to a slight variation in moisture content.

It is further reported that scientifically established methods are available for reducing the moisture content and that such methods may be adopted to bring the product into full compliance with the prescribed standards.
The analysis report dated 08.01.2026 and the Food Analyst's report dated 12.01.2026 have been produced before us by the learned Government Pleader.
The Registry is directed to incorporate the reports of the Analysts along with the Sabarimala Special Commissioner's Report.

4. Having regard to the contents of the report, we find that although the honey contains a marginally excess moisture content and has accordingly been declared non-conforming, the Analyst has clearly stated that the product may be permitted to undergo reprocessing using scientifically established methods.

In view of the same, we deem it appropriate to direct that such scientifically established methods shall be employed without delay to reduce the moisture content, under the presence and supervision of the Food Safety Officer.
Thereafter, upon ensuring through appropriate testing that the honey is no longer substandard and conforms to the prescribed standards, the same may be put to use.

As the Food Safety Officer has insisted that the product must be re-tested after the reduction of moisture by established methods, the SSCR NO. 2 OF 2026     :5:  
2026:KER:2813
additional
8th respondent shall ensure that such testing is carried out within 24 hours so that the large quantity of honey is not wasted.
The Sabarimala Special Commissioner's Report is disposed of.
